main_text.head: FLORUM HORTULI HISTORICO-POLITICI
CORONA IV.
De subditorum officio, & splendida ministrorum aulicorum miseria.
FLOS I.
DEUM time: Regem honora.
I.Petri c.2.
main_text.p: MUTUATUS videtur hunc aphorismum Petrus Apostolus ex Salomonis Regis sapientissimi Proverbiorum c.14. Time Deum ac Regem: quo utroque aphorismo primùm praecipitur, ut Deum, à quo omnia, per quem omnia, & in quo sunt omnia, ante omnia timeamus & revereamur.

Basis enim omnis felicitatis & virtutis est θεοσεβείας & mater σοφίας omniúsq; virtutis est timere DEUM, Timorù Domini effectus. secundùm illud Iobi cap.28. vel, ut Siracides in suo Ecclesiastico cap.1. multis verbis ejusdem effectus recenset, Timor Domini est decus & gloria, laetitia & pulcerrima corona, gaudio & laetitia perfundens cor, radices agens sapientia in cordibus credentium: quae donis suis universam domum replet, &, omnia receptacula thesauris suis: imò corona est sapientia, uberrimam pacem & salutem afferens, amplissimaq; gloria eos ornans, & ad summum auctoritatis fastigium evehens, insuperq; prudentiam largè in eos effundens, à quibus diligitur: ut videre est in

page.notes: The Greek words in the second paragraph (θεοσεβείας, σοφίας) are read with some uncertainty because the scan is faint. The Latin of the Ecclesiasticus quotation is italic in the printing. The margin note reads "T.morù" in the scan; the first word is taken as "Timorù" with doubt. The catchword at the foot is cut off on the scan, so "Iosi" may be an incomplete word. The hyphen in "recen-set" at the line end is printed and is kept by joining the word. The line "Timor Domini" at the start of the note is cut at the margin.
